# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 1 | **Condition:** heavily damaged

---

**1** [...] You are the God who knows all things. Every true thought has its origin in You, and every righteous intention comes from Your presence. [...]

**2** [...] Nothing happens without You. Nothing is known apart from what You will. No one stands beside You, no one [...]

**3** [...] Nothing compares with Your glory. Your power is beyond all measure. Who, among all Your astonishing works, [...]

**4** [...] could ever contain Your glory? What are human beings among Your wonders? How can anyone born of a woman dare to stand in Your presence? [...]

**5** [...] We are kneaded from dust — and worm-food is our destiny. We are shaped from clay, and to dust we return. [...]

**6** [...] How could clay ever understand? What can a thing made from dirt figure out on its own? How could it even take a single step? [...] Yet You have established [...]

**7** [...] Everything You have done, You have done for Your glory. [...] a spirit trapped in flesh [...] an eternal purpose [...]

**8** [...] to walk in everything You love, to turn away from everything You hate, and to do what is right in Your eyes. [...]

**9** [...] You have poured out Your Holy Spirit on Your servant [...] to wash him clean from every evil deed. [...]

**10** [...] out of Your overflowing compassion, out of the depths of Your mercy — for all who belong to Your truth. [...]

**11** [...] You have opened a spring to cleanse the stained [...] a pool of purification for those weighed down by guilt. [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 1 is a meditation on the gulf between God's infinite knowledge and human frailty — and then, stunningly, the bridge: God's Holy Spirit poured out to purify. The "kneaded from dust / food of worms" imagery is visceral and should be felt, not smoothed. The shift from despair (lines 4-6) to grace (lines 9-11) is the emotional arc of the fragment. PNEUMA renders the surviving text to let that arc land, using modern idiom without losing the raw force of Qumran Hebrew.*

— PNEUMA
